title: SDK first-mile guides and playflow notes
content:
Purpose:

This note captures a compact, opinionated set of artifacts and flows for the very first minutes developers spend with Redwood SDKs — the ‘first mile’. The goal is to reduce time-to-success from signup to a working request in under 5 minutes, and then a production-ready sample in under an hour.

Audience:
- New engineers evaluating Redwood for a prototype or POC
- Internal SDK maintainers and docs writers
- Solutions engineers running customer pilots

Outcomes we care about (measurable):
- 5-minute success rate: percent of test users who get a generation or embedding call working within 5 minutes of hitting the quickstart
- 60-minute demo loop: percent who can wire the SDK into a tiny app (web or CLI) within 60 minutes without help
- Telemetry coverage: default SDK captures the three core metrics (latency, tokens, model) and sends to Console by default in dev mode
- Reduction in support tickets about "how do I make my first call" by 50% for new accounts in the trial cohort

Constraints and guiding principles:
- Keep the first-mile path single-threaded and deterministic (minimal branching, one clear path for Node/Python/CLI)
- Avoid heavy config or infra: prefer SDKs that use a hosted endpoint and an API key for the quickstart; defer Dedicated/Private flows to separate docs
- Provide a one-file canonical example per platform that can be copy-pasted and run locally (no build step where possible)
- Make failures obvious and actionable (clear error text + link to next step)

Deliverables (initial sprint):
1) One-page README: "Run a request in 3 steps" with copy-paste snippets for Node, Python, and a tiny shell curl example.
2) Three single-file canonical sample apps:
   - node-hello-redwood.js (no deps other than node 18+; uses fetch or a tiny helper)
   - py_hello_redwood.py (python 3.10; uses requests only)
   - rwi-cli (bash one-liner + tiny helper script for interactive prompts)
3) Starter repo: /sdk-starters with the three examples and minimal tests (smoke-only) + GH issue template for problems during quickstart
4) Telemetry contract doc: what the SDK emits by default (event names, required tags, opt-out knobs)
5) Short video (90s) that demonstrates the 3-step flow (for marketing and support)

Opinionated quickstart flow (the canonical path) — keep this as small as possible:
- Step 0: Create account + copy API key (UI shows the minimal token with example curl)
- Step 1: Paste key into environment: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx
- Step 2: Copy-paste single-file example for your language and run: node node-hello-redwood.js
- Step 3: See response; follow link to "Next steps" which is a tiny checklist: add SDK to package, add telemetry, try streaming, pin a model version.

Example single-file content notes (we will keep these in the repo; include short variants in README):
- Node example uses global fetch and prints the generation text; on error it prints a short remediation list (bad key, network, account not activated).
- Python example is interactive: prompts for prompt text if none supplied on CLI.
- Bash curl example demonstrates minimal headers + JSON body for text generation.

Samples and templates for tiny apps (1-hour targets):
- Web demo: static HTML + JS using fetch to call a small proxy included in the starter repo (so we don’t expose API keys in-browser); the proxy is a single express file.
- CLI generator: a 1-file node CLI using yargs to accept prompt, model, and temperature; includes a --stream flag to demonstrate streaming tokens to stdout.
- Slack bot skeleton: minimal express webhook receiver that calls Redwood and posts back summarized results (used by solutions eng for quick demos).

Telemetry & gating (default SDK behavior in quickstart):
- Default: emit non-PII telemetry in dev mode containing: sdk.name, sdk.version, language, region, model, request_latency_ms, request_token_count, sample_rate (configurable).
- Opt-out: environment variable REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0 disables sending.
- Console mapping: we should wire sample events into the Console under "Quickstart telemetry" so we can measure the 5-minute success rate (heuristic: a sequence of events: sdk:start -> request:success).
- Gating for enterprise: for Dedicated/Private quickstarts, telemetry must be explicit opt-in in the onboarding flow; provide an onboarding toggle in Console.

Error messaging conventions (short list to standardize across SDKs):
- Auth errors: concise reason + link to UI to rotate key + example curl snippet to test
- Quota/limit errors: show specific quota and link to upgrade flow
- Bad payload: include field names and minimal example payload that will work
- Network/timeouts: show recommended retry/backoff snippet (sane default 2 retries)

Docs placement and nav suggestions:
- One canonical page under Product Docs: "First Mile SDK guide" with 3 tabs for Node/Python/CLI and inline copy-paste samples.
- Starter repo README should surface the video and the single-file examples at the top.
- Keep the longer how-tos (streaming, embeddings, function calling) as separate pages linked from "Next steps" — don’t overload the first-mile page.

Milestones (6-week plan):
Week 1: finalize single-file examples, land starter repo, basic README.
Week 2: add telemetry contract and small smoke tests, update SDKs to emit required events.
Week 3: video recording + walkthrough, GH issue templates, user testing with internal new-hire cohort.
Week 4: polish error messages, integrate quickstart telemetry into Console dashboards (basic).
Week 5: iterate from internal feedback, fix friction points; prepare marketing brief.
Week 6: soft launch to trial cohort, monitor metrics and collect bug reports.

Risks and open questions (to decide quickly):
- How opinionated should default model/version selection be for first-mile? (we lean to a small curated set, not latest always)
- Should the single-file examples use the official SDK packages or just raw curl/fetch? (tradeoff: SDK shows best path but adds dependency friction)
- Telemetry privacy expectations for trial users in Europe — legal wants explicit notice in UI. Need TOC with Legal.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: create starter repo skeleton and push node/python/bash single-file examples (due: +10d)
- Diego: prototype telemetry events in node SDK and open PR (due: +12d)
- Priya: script + record 90s demo video and draft README captions (due: +14d)
- Ethan: add smoke GH actions and minimal test that runs the examples with a mocked endpoint (due: +14d)

Notes to self / loose ideas (brainstorm fragments):
- Consider an interactive "first-run" CLI that walks users through setting env var and running the example (could be nice for demos in workshops).
- Add a tiny badge generator that shows "📦 SDK ready: 3-min quickstart" for README files.
- Collect a small set of community prompts to demonstrate typical usage in docs (customer-facing examples).

If you want to dive in: link to starter repo (TODO) and ping me in #devex for pairing on the first demo run.
